agent_notes: הַבֵּיט / וּרְאֵה: forms are imperatives (YLT and ASV/BBE split: imperative to God vs. the poet's own look). Radak and Ibn Ezra read them as infinitives ('looking ... and seeing'), Meiri as a call to God. I rendered them as an imperative to God, which fits the verb's tone of petition and the flow into v.6, and noted the alternative in the commentary.

מַכִּיר: 'one who recognizes me', i.e. who acknowledges me; KJV 'know me' is acceptable but 'acknowledge' catches the legal-social sense. The gloss is my own reading; HALOT lists the sense 'to take notice of, acknowledge'.

agent_notes: יַכְתִּרוּ: hapax-like Hiphil of כתר 'to surround/crown'. Rashi and Ibn Ezra take it as 'crown', Radak as 'make me a crown', ASV/KJV as 'surround'. I kept 'will surround' (STEPBible) in the glosses and mention 'crown' in the commentary and notes; the Hiphil form with a Qal-like sense is a point I make no claim on beyond the commentaries.
תִגְמֹל עָלָי: 'deal bountifully' follows STEPBible; the root גמל is neutral ('deal fully with') and takes a positive sense here from context, as in Ps 13:6 and 116:7.

notes.note: Нумерация: в Синодальном переводе (Пс 141) надписание не нумеруется, поэтому наш стих 2 соответствует его стиху 1, и так далее до конца псалма. Так же сдвинута нумерация в KJV; в комментариях это сказано.
